findings.title: Executable-owner authoring is ordered after final source and install proof
findings.problem: The packet explicitly presents ten ordered barriers. Stage1 requires reviewed full-clause case-to-assertion owners; stages3/4 freeze exact combined committed source and obtain fresh source→artifact→installed-entry proof; stage7 then instructs authoring the full251 executable ownership. The order does not distinguish pre-freeze ownership authoring from execution of already-frozen owners, or require re-entering existing freeze/proof barriers when later authoring changes source or packaged manifest/fixture bytes.
findings.impact: The literal sequence can require rebuilding/rebinding an installation after stage7, or confuse which owner/artifact bytes earlier proof covered. All identities and execution remain CLOSED/UNKNOWN, so this is planning precision, not a demonstrated gate bypass, runtime failure or grant of credit.
findings.smallestFix: Complete executable-owner authoring/review and manifest/fixture input freeze before the final combined-source/artifact freeze and fresh install proof; stage7 executes those already-frozen owners. Alternatively explicitly return through the same existing freeze/proof barriers for every post-proof byte change. Preserve selected laws, semantics, source ownership, budgets and no-retry policy; add no new gate or report-union mechanism.
findings.sourceBasis: Existing artifact bundle copies/digests exact catalog/manifest/fixture inputs; runner executes those frozen scenarios, and installed baseline binds exact payload/fixture/source identity. Later authoring cannot be attributed to prior bytes.

scope: FULL independent native contract precision; closed preparation only
